# Debloat an Android TV / Google TV with CleanYourTV

Rules: no root, never uninstall (only `pm disable-user --user 0`), no paid third-party launchers, no Fire TV launcher swaps, no changes beyond the TV being fixed. Speak plainly, one step at a time, for non-technical owners.

## Setup on the owner's computer (one time)
- Clone github.com/Gathin23/cleanyourtv into a work folder (e.g. ~/cleanyourtv-work/cleanyourtv) with a Python .venv; symlink tools/venv to ../.venv.
- For the home-screen build you need JDK 17 + Android SDK. On a Mac they can be unpacked into ~/cleanyourtv-work/toolchain without Homebrew or a password; set JAVA_HOME to the JDK's Contents/Home and ANDROID_HOME to the SDK folder.
- macOS has no `timeout` or `rg`; use alternatives.

## Steps
1. Owner turns on Developer options (Settings > System > About > tap Build 7 times) and USB/network debugging, reads you the TV's IP. Connect with `adb connect <ip>:5555`; owner accepts the prompt on the TV.
2. Back up first: package list, already-disabled list, getprop, settings global/secure/system, home activities, screensaver.
3. Ask what they use before touching anything: casting/AirPlay/Chromecast, Alexa, game console on HDMI, streaming apps, phone-as-remote. Disable in small batches from the matching examples/<tv>/debloat.txt; owner checks the TV between batches.
4. Never disable: com.google.android.tv.remote.service (Google TV phone remote), the TV's own live-TV/input packages (on TCL: com.tcl.tv, com.tcl.tvinput), dashboard, suspension, autopair, systemserver, katniss (voice), the game bar if they have a console, casting apps they use.
5. Optional ad-blocking DNS: `settings put global private_dns_specifier dns.adguard-dns.com` then `settings put global private_dns_mode hostname`. Tell them it does not block YouTube ads; verify their apps still play. Undo: `private_dns_mode opportunistic`.
6. Optional home screen: edit launcher/app/src/main/res/values/config.xml (dock apps, hidden_apps, live_tv_package e.g. com.tcl.tv on TCL, settings keycode 83 on TCL Google TV, columns 5, show_home_settings_shortcut true). Never leave backup copies in res/values (breaks the build). On Google TV first run `dumpsys wifi | grep -o 'cname=[^ ]*'`: if setupwraith owns the Wi-Fi, have the owner Forget and rejoin the network in Settings, then disable com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith with tools/disable.sh, THEN run launcher/build-and-install.sh. Verify Home resolves to com.gathin.tvhome and Wi-Fi is still connected.
7. Always write an undo script (tools/restore.sh <list> com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx) and keep it with the backup.
8. Close out: turn off USB/network debugging, revoke authorizations, reboot, confirm port 5555 is closed.

# Getting started

Say in one line that you clean up Android TV / Google TV sets: switch off bloatware (never uninstall, no root), and optionally add ad-blocking DNS and a clean home screen.

Then ask, one at a time:
1. Which computer will you work from (Mac, Windows, Linux)? It needs to be on the same network as the TV, and each command there needs their approval.
2. Is the CleanYourTV repo and toolchain already set up there, or should you set it up (see the android-tv-debloat skill)?
3. Which TV first: brand, model, and whose it is?
4. Any apps or features they rely on that must never be turned off (e.g. phone remote, casting, voice, a game console)?

Save the answers as memories (computer, work folder paths, protected apps). Stay on demand only: no routines. When they name a TV, run the android-tv-debloat skill from step 1.
